ucs.title: [LLM] Turla ComRAT/Carbon C2 hidden inside Gmail & Google web-service traffic
ucs.description: Hunts for ComRAT v4 (a.k.a. Chinch) and related Turla implants that abuse the legitimate Gmail web UI / Google API endpoints for bidirectional C2 — commands are read from an attacker mailbox and results uploaded as attachments. Turla characteristically routes C2 through trusted web services to blend with normal traffic, so the tell is a NON-browser process (injected svchost/explorer/rundll32 or an AppData/ProgramData binary) reaching Google mail endpoints.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_host IN ("mail.google.com","www.googleapis.com","accounts.google.com","googleapis.com") AND NOT All_Traffic.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","opera.exe","safari.exe") AND NOT All_Traffic.process_name="" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("mail.google.com","www.googleapis.com","accounts.google.com","googleapis.com")
// ComRAT impersonates the Gmail UI but rides on a non-browser host process
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("svchost.exe","rundll32.exe","explorer.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","dllhost.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmiprvse.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\appdata\", @"\programdata\", @"\windows\temp\", @"\users\public\")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Hits=count(), Ports=make_set(RemotePort), IPs=make_set(RemoteIP)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl
| order by LastSeen desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Turla ComRAT C2 via Google Web Service from Non-Browser Process
id: 7c2f0a4e-3d61-4f8e-9c2a-2f1b8b6a9d10
status: experimental
description: Detects non-browser processes resolving/connecting to Gmail and Google API endpoints, consistent with Turla ComRAT v4 web-service C2.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0010/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_domain:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'mail.google.com'
      - 'www.googleapis.com'
      - 'accounts.google.com'
  filter_browsers:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
      - '\opera.exe'
  condition: selection_domain and not filter_browsers
falsepositives:
  - Custom internal tooling or backup agents legitimately calling Google APIs
level: high
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1102.002
  - attack.g0010
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(mail.google.com OR www.googleapis.com OR accounts.google.com OR googleapis.com) -@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\Chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\MsEdge.exe OR *\firefox.exe OR *\Firefox.exe OR *\iexplore.exe OR *\IEXPLORE.EXE OR *\brave.exe OR *\opera.exe)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(mail\.google\.com|www\.googleapis\.com|accounts\.google\.com|googleapis\.com)/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/(chrome|msedge|firefox|iexplore|brave|opera|safari)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| count > 0

ucs.title: [LLM] Turla registry-resident PowerShell loader (PowerShellRunner / Kazuar stager)
ucs.description: Hunts Turla's fileless PowerShell loader pattern where an encrypted .NET payload is stashed in a registry value and reflectively loaded at runtime — the chain reads a blob via Get-ItemProperty/reg, Base64/AES-decodes it, and reflectively loads the assembly with IEX. This is the staging mechanism Turla (Secret Blizzard / Venomous Bear) uses to deploy Kazuar and PowerShellRunner-managed backdoors while keeping payloads off disk.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND Processes.process IN ("*Get-ItemProperty*","*Get-Item *","*reg query*","*gp HK*") AND Processes.process IN ("*FromBase64String*","*IEX*","*Invoke-Expression*","*Reflection.Assembly*","*[Reflection.Assembly]::Load*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
// step 1: pulls the payload out of a registry value (fileless storage)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Get-ItemProperty","Get-Item ","reg query","gp HKCU","gp HKLM","HKCU:\\Software","HKLM:\\Software")
// step 2: decodes + reflectively loads the .NET assembly in-memory
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("FromBase64String","IEX","Invoke-Expression","Reflection.Assembly","[Reflection.Assembly]::Load",".Invoke(")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("Get-ItemProperty","Get-Item ","reg query","gp HKCU","gp HKLM","HKCU:\\Software","HKLM:\\Software")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("FromBase64String","IEX","Invoke-Expression","Reflection.Assembly","[Reflection.Assembly]::Load",".Invoke(")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Turla PowerShell Registry-Resident Reflective Loader
id: 1b9d44c2-6e7a-4a0f-bf2e-9d3c5f1e0a22
status: experimental
description: Detects PowerShell that reads a payload from a registry value and reflectively loads/decodes it in-memory, matching Turla PowerShellRunner/Kazuar staging.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0010/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ps:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_regread:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Get-ItemProperty'
      - 'Get-Item '
      - 'reg query'
      - 'HKCU:\Software'
      - 'HKLM:\Software'
  selection_load:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - 'IEX'
      - 'Invoke-Expression'
      - 'Reflection.Assembly'
      - '[Reflection.Assembly]::Load'
  condition: selection_ps and selection_regread and selection_load
falsepositives:
  - Some endpoint management / installer scripts cache and load config from registry
level: high
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1027.011
  - attack.t1112
  - attack.g0010
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:((*Get-ItemProperty* OR *Get-Item* OR *reg\ query* OR *HKCU:\Software* OR *HKLM:\Software*) AND (*FromBase64String* OR *IEX* OR *Invoke-Expression* OR *Reflection.Assembly*))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(Get-ItemProperty|Get-Item |reg query|HK(CU|LM):\\\\Software)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(?i)(FromBase64String|IEX|Invoke-Expression|Reflection\\.Assembly|\\[Reflection\\.Assembly\\]::Load)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
| count > 0
ucs.rationale: Turla's PowerShellRunner and Kazuar loaders are documented for keeping AES/Base64-encrypted .NET payloads inside registry values and reflectively loading them, a deliberate fileless-storage choice (T1027.011) to defeat disk-based AV — tracked by Microsoft as Secret Blizzard and CrowdStrike as Venomous Bear. The detection fires only on the specific combination of registry-value read + in-memory ref
